- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon — if forecast is >+2% above recent 10d average, reduce by 10–15%.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.67/1.00 entries followed by 0.33/0.00, model tends to “forget” recent highs; add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to compensate.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show rising prices, model often fails to capture continuation; add 0.5–1.5% lagged momentum bias.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33/0.67 alternating), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
